Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Wysox Township

Inspection Date: 6/05/2025
Comments: On 04/17/2025 the DEP conducted a routine inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) Them Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) 1.8-3.45 mS/cm. The DEP collected samples. On 05/07/2025 the DEP received the sample results from the discovered release. Based on sample results the following violations were cited against API #015-23911:35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b). Due to the unknown quantity of the release this was referred to Act 2 for compliance.On 06/05/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) Them Well Pad. The weather was 80 degrees and sunny. Expand Representative Mike Deming accompanied me during the inspection. Pooled water in the area of the discovered release was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 980-1600 us/cm. The soil was also field measured for EC between 500-700 us/cm. Mike stated a vacuum truck would be onsite by end of day to recover the elevated water. The puddles that need to be recovered were marked.The following violations remain open against API #015-23911:35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8203141
Permit API: 129-23976
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/27/2024
Comments: On September 27 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Louis Yemc 1 Well in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County.At the time of the inspection, the well was reported to be plugged (according to Department records) with no monument present. The access road appears to be unrestored. Documentation submitted to the Department by the Operator for the access road to remain is currently under review by the Department. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. There appears to be no residual waste or plugging material left on the well site since the pad is no longer there. Equipment has been left onsite. The former site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the recently dug pit for the removal of the pit contents. The Department recommends that the Operator place BMPs downslope of the recently dug pit to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues. Plugging was completed on 12/08/2023 (according to Department records), therefore the site must be restored no later than 9/8/2024. The well site restoration report shall be issued within 60 days after restoration of the well site in accordance with 78.65(3).Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to have temporary E and S BMPs installed to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues, and for failure to have site restored.

properties.content:
Report Details

Permit API: 129-27503
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-02-03
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to inspection 2975784 conducted on 12/20/2019 in response to a leak from one of the Production Tanks reported by a PADEP OGI inspector. The Act 9 Sign is present. The Department recommends that the operator maintains the sign to ensure that its contents remain easily visible. The ERP is in the mailbox and is site specific. The site appears constructed and equipped for production with x2 Production Tanks in an earthen dike, x2 separators and the well fenced off. The well is labeled, no leaks, dead or distressed vegetation observed. The Production Tanks are both labeled as "Not In Use." Both appear to be covered in corrosion. No holes visually discernible. The Department advises the operator that they must have the land owners permission to keep such equipment on site, otherwise it should be removed. The impacted area appears to be remediated, with visibly impacted stone removed and replaced. No leaks observed around Production Tanks. There appears to be an animal hole in the earthen dike. The Department recommends that the operator exclude the animal and maintain the dike. No response has been received by the Department in reference to inspection 2975784. As such the Department is again requesting maintenance logs for the Production Tanks and a timeline for when the operator is planning to remove or fix the Production Tanks. Based on this inspection, and no received response on information requested regarding the brine release, all violations will remain open. The Department recommends that the operator monitor the site for distressed vegetation. The Department also requests disposal records and a waste manifest for any contaminated materials removed from the site in response to this release. Further violations may be forthcoming based on responses received by the operator.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 941176
Permit API: 081-21796
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Hepburn Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 1/06/2022
Comments: On January 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an administrative inspection for a spill at the Inflection Energy Hensler Well Pad. On January 5, 2022, around 2140, Zac Subra reported a spill of approximately 30 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the well pad surface. At about 920 on January 6, 2022, DEP spoke with Zac Subra on the phone. Mr. Subra said a hydraulic fluid line on a water truck ruptured and caused the spill. Inflection contractors began removing the hydraulic fluid and excavating the impacted soil immediately. Inflection contractors excavated an area of about 20 ft. X 15 ft. of the pad surface. Due to the ground being frozen, Inflection contractors only had to scrape the top of the pad surface to remove the impacted soil in the previously noted area. The impacted soil was added to a rolloff dumpster and hauled to a landfill. Inflection then went back to the pad during the day to verify that the impacted soil had been completely removed. Zac said a small amount of remaining soil had to be removed at this time since it was not observed earlier in the morning. The small amount of soil was added to barrels and is awaiting approval to be disposed of. Inflection then backfilled the excavated area with clean fill. Photos of the area excavated and clean up were provided by Inflection Energy. The spill of hydraulic fluid outside of containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.54. The violations have been immediately corrected.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Brokenstraw Township, Warren County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/15/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Brokenstraw Township, Warren county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/15/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8278409
Permit API: 123-45905
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/15/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Conklin Lease tank battery. Mature trees at the southwest corner of the secondary containment area are either heavily stressed or dead. A brine tank is buried within the secondary containment area. PVC lines connect the drain valves of the stock tanks in containment to cutout holes in the surface of the brine tank. Evidence of previous fluid releases in the containment area are visible via crude oil staining and sawdust sprinkled over the oil-stained areas. It appears that the PVC lines connected to the two stock tanks in the southernmost end of the containment area have been the most heavily used. At the time of this inspection, the PVC lines are placed inside the cutout holes of the brine tank. However, oil-staining, visible wetness, and sawdust sprinkled around these cutout holes indicate that at one time fluid was allowed to run over the surface of the brine tank and onto the ground within the secondary containment area. Elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 3,000 uS/cm was observed beneath both of the aforementioned PVC lines.A pool of fluid was present in the southernmost end of the containment area, in what appeared to be a sump. At the time of this inspection, the fluid was observed to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 4,000 uS/cm. Soils at the bottom of the sump also had elevated specific conductance which measured in excess of 11,000 uS/cm. The floor of the secondary containment area above the sump was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 uS/cm. A drainage swale is located approximately 30 feet west of the secondary containment area wall. Upslope soil conductivity readings in the swale were observed at 96 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance in excess of 4,000 uS/cm was observed in soils within the swale directly across from the tank battery. Crude oil staining was also observed in the swale near the tank battery. The swale transitions to an UNT to Irvine Run with defined bed and banks downslope of the tank battery. The water flowing in the UNT was found to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 13,000 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance of water was observed throughout the stream at the time of this inspection. The specific conductance of water in the stream was observed to drop below 1,000 uS/cm after two confluences with apparently unaffected sources of fresh water at a point approximately 200 feet north of a culvert and the lease road which crosses the UNT. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Conklin lease.

Permit API: 083-46720
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2026
Comments: I conducted a follow up inspection of this conventional well that had a release occur in November of 2025, when a steel gathering line had ruptured resulting in crude oil contaminating ditches and soil. Initially the remediation of the site was progressing. There had been no signs of product at the under flow dams, there was no viable oil in the ditches. In preperation of obtaining confirmatory soil samples to evaluate if the remediation was sufficient, it was discovered another leak had developed on a different section of the same line. This operator indicated they will replace all of the steel line for this well with plastic/poly line. This release was caught early and as of now, appears to be less than 1 bbl of lost product and has impacted a minimal amount of soil.Bull Run employees had a roll off dumpster en-route to remove the impacted soil. The ruptured line was sucked out with a vac truck and will be removed while running new poly line. Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/01/2025 to CNX GAS CO LLC in West Finley Township, Washington county. 78A73(C)___ - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION – The operator failed to immediately electronically notify the Department of any change to a well being monitored, of any treatment pressure or volume changes indicative of abnormal fracture propagation at the well being stimulated or if otherwise made aware of a confirmed well communication incident associated with their stimulation activities.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CNX GAS CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/01/2025
Violation Code: 78A73(C)___ - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION – The operator failed to immediately electronically notify the Department of any change to a well being monitored, of any treatment pressure or volume changes indicative of abnormal fracture propagation at the well being stimulated or if otherwise made aware of a confirmed well communication incident associated with their stimulation activities.
Violation ID: 8257904
Permit API: 125-29137
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: West Finley Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/01/2025
Comments: The Department was on site to conduct an inspection of the CNX WFN12HHSM. CNX had reported a casing failure on 11/26/2025 at 9:41pm while fracking this well. They were zipper fracking 3 wells at time of incident. The other 2 wells being fracked were the WFN12GHSM and the WFN13JHSM. WFN12GHSM was on stage 54 of 64 and the WFN12JHSM 41 of 53. CNX was on stage 52 of 64 on the WFN12HHSM when they observed a pressure failure. On the WFN12HHSMN, stage 52 began at 11:01am on Wednesday November 26, 2025. CNX observed a pressure loss at 11:23am. CNX was pumping at 9600psi at the time of the pressure loss. 3600psi was observed on the 5x9 and the 9x13 annuli immediately after shutting down. The pop-offs were set at 900 psi. The company man did confirm they had flow on the 5x9 annuli. The 5x9 pressure equalized to around 524psi after plugs were set inside the 5 1/2" (5 1/2" production casing, 5x9 annuli, and the 9x13" annuli). Pressure was bled off after the incident when the pressure reached 200psi. The pressure on both annuli are currently at 0psi as of today's inspection. They didn't see any pressure on the wells today after bleeding off the pressure last night. 2 composite bridge plugs were set at 7701' and 7404'. CNX finished fracking the other 2 wells after the bridge plugs were set. A 60 arm caliper and a Dark Vision Log were ran on this well. CNX is awaiting the results of these logs. The communication incident occurred on 11/26/2025 at 11:23am and CNX did not report the incident to the Department until 9:41pm, which is a violation of 78a73(c) for failure to immediately notify the Department of any change to a well being monitored, of any treatment pressures or volume changes indicative of abnormal fracture propagation at the well being stimulated or if otherwise made aware of a confirmed well communication associated with their stimulation activities. Following notification, Technical Guidance Document (TGD) 800-0810-001, Guidelines for implementing Area of Review (AOR) Regulatory Requirement for Unconventional Wells, describes the incident report that should be electronically filed within 3 days of the incident. The Department has not received the AOR Fracture Communication Incident Report. The Department requests CNX to submit that report. As per the Pressure Barrier Policy (PBP), unconventional operators should report all well control incidents/losses of well control and well control emergencies within 2 hours of confirmation to the Department. In addition, notification should have been provided to the coal Operator (sensitive offset environments). The Department has not received a PBP notification.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2022
Violation Code: OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
Violation ID: 948143
Permit API: 047-24640
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This unconventional well is currently equipped for production and is equipped with a well tag displaying the well’s API number. The site ID sign at the entrance of the pad includes the required information, however it has become faded. Drilling operations were completed on this well on 12/10/2011. There is a second active well (047-24639) on this pad for which drilling operations were completed on 11/13/2011. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0025 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling the last permitted well on this well site. Approximately one-third of this pad does not appear to be actively used for the operation of this well. There are four steel tanks labeled as holding production water located inside of a lined steel containment on this well site. At this time, the containment appears sound, as it is holding several inches of stormwater. The access road leading to this well site and well development impoundment is in general holding up to current traffic levels. There are isolated areas of scouring that should be addressed in an effort to avoid potential E&S issues in the future. Routine maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road given its proximity to Bear Creek, Little Wolf Run and several unnamed tributaries. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site & well development impoundment, as well as the access road banks appears to be established. Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site & well development impoundment.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 2019-11-04

Permit API: 035-21316
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton

Comments: I arrived on site and met Nate Veneziano, Clint Stoltzfus, and George Winebark of XTO. Zachary Lieb and Brynn Yochim of Moody & Associates were also present. Sitewide containment was being removed and the pad screened to identify areas in need of excavation due to the produced water release identified on 5/28/19 by Brad Kline, WQS for the Department. Containment removal began to the north of the wellheads, working clockwise around them. Zach and Brynn began their conductivity screening on the west edge of the pad where high conductance fluid was moving off the pad; distressed vegetation in this area appears to have recovered. Very little water was present on the north side of the wellheads, and soil and water conductance in this area was low (.2-.4 mS/cm) with the exception of an area bare of gravel approximately 10' east by northeast of the wells. This area showed soil conductance of 1.98 mS/cm. To the east of the wellheads, what appeared to be several petroleum stains were present, and one very small (less than 1 quart) puddle showed high conductance (16.50 mS/cm). Other puddles in close proximity showed low conductance (.65-1.2 mS/cm). To the south of the wells between the wells and the produced water Baker tank battery, water was puddled nearly everywhere; conductance reading were low (.185-.235 mS/cm). When I departed, containment had not yet been removed to the west of the wellheads; as this was the potential flow path of the release, this area should be screened thoroughly.

Three roll-off containers remain on-site, and it appears that remediation has been completed. No soil sample documentation has been received by the Department as of this date, and heavy deer tracks at the restored site indicate that there may still be some residual contamination. All documentation regarding the Act 2 clean-up of this site should be submitted to the Department as soon as it is available.The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The well valves were closed at the time of inspection, and the 50 bbl brine tank appears to be empty. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 12/6/2023 (Inspection Record # 3655836), there have been no changes at the site. New violations have been issued during this inspection for failure to comply with an issued court order, failure to plug the well upon abandonment, and for failure to submit annual production information.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in New Vernon Twp, Mercer County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/02/2022 to DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in New Vernon Twp, Mercer county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/02/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 954016
Permit API: 085-22185
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: New Vernon Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/02/2022
Comments: Responded to an oil spill at this gas well location. The plug for the heater tube in the stock tank failed and allowed oil to leak out of the tank and into the diking. With the recent heavy rains, it appears the fluid in the diking overflowed through an open freshwater drain pipe and an inadequate diking height in spots. There was a ditch located on the backside of the diking where some of the oil flowed into but most of the oil appears to have gone out the freshwater drain pipe and then down the lease road. The lease road was approximately 55 yards long and pockets of oil were located throughout it and then into the weeds heading towards that same ditch that runs parallel to the lease road. The ditch empties into the Lake Wilhelm Road ditch. This Lake Wilhelm Road ditch just had a sheen of oil of oil on it west of the driveway. The last spot oil was seen in this ditch was about 10 yards east of the driveway culvert pipe outfall. No oil or sheen was seen emptying into or in the main stream of Calvin Clark Run itself. The oil was mostly contained with sorbent pads and by the grass and brush in the ditch. Based on site observations, it appears that less than 1 bbl of oil was released outside the diking area. With the heavy rains predicted again in the next 2 days, it was suggested for them to install a siphon dam in the field ditch right before it enters into the road ditch. A small excavator arrived on site and was in the process of doing this when I left. They were getting a vac truck out there today to remove all the fluid in the tank to stop the leaking of the oil. At 3:31 PM, Matt Kleese from Diamond Energy called me. He reported that they had just removed around 50 bbls of old motor oil from that stock tank. He said this well produces very little fluid and it was definitely old oil (he thinks motor oil). So he feels somebody had apparently dumped old motor oil in this tank. He said that he is probably going to file a police report on this incident.
